quotes.text: When an agent borrows a login, every action it takes looks like the person who owns that login did it. And that turns your audit trail into a work of fiction.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Vividly shows why agents need their own identity.

quotes.text: It doesn't hold credentials at all, which means there's nothing sitting on the agent that an attacker could steal, and the agent can't sign in by itself.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the key security design of agent identities.

quotes.text: When you disable a blueprint, every agent identity underneath it stops signing in immediately, which makes it a genuine kill switch.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows the governance power concentrated in the blueprint.

quotes.text: Don't judge an agent by a single permission. Add up everything it can do across roles, tools and systems because that total is the real power the agent holds
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical security habit for assessing agent permissions.

quotes.text: The common thread is simple agents are easy to create and easy to forget, and every one of these pitfalls comes from forgetting that an agent is an identity you have to look after.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the root cause behind all the pitfalls.

chapters.title: Agent vs. service principal vs. managed identity

takeaways: Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives each AI agent its own identity with a named human sponsor, so you can tell which agent did what and who is responsible.
Agent identities hold no credentials; the blueprint holds them, which makes the blueprint both a powerful kill switch and a high-value target to protect.
Govern agents with agent-specific Conditional Access policies, sponsors, access packages, lifecycle policies and least-privilege permissions.
hook: AI agents are signing in to Microsoft 365 tenants with borrowed or shared accounts nobody can name, which breaks audit trails and accountability. This episode explains Microsoft Entra Agent ID, blueprints, sponsors and how agent identities differ from service principals and managed identities. Identity and security admins learn how to govern agents with Conditional Access, lifecycle policies and least privilege.
